A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DUS research, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison. All seven pages of v1 and nine pages of v3 were inspected, including v3's Appendices A.1–A.2; v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: Table 1 reports original DUS and confidence-planner experiments using three diffusion models on GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and reports additional benchmark, DiffuCoder, scheduling-ablation, and block-size results in Tables 1–3 and 5.

M1.justification: The core dilation rule, final-group merging, and optional confidence-based skipping remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds a limited inference adaptation: starting DUS at iteration t0 > 1 to reveal larger groups within a fixed computation budget.

E1.justification: V3 retains GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP while adding MATH500 and subsets of BBH and MMLU-Pro. This substantially extends coverage to harder mathematics and general reasoning/professional-knowledge questions.

E2.justification: The main DUS-versus-confidence comparison remains. V3 adds random sampling and incremental confidence/random variants in Table 3, and evaluates entropy-based confidence for DiffuCoder. These are targeted additions; the single-token and AR reference baselines in Figure 1 are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds DiffuCoder Base/Instruct configurations and GSM8K protocols using 300 examples to compare schedules or vary block size at fixed total NFE=32. DiffuCoder's baseline explicitly disables semi-AR. Section 4.1 also introduces k=B/log2(B), but later passages retain k=log2(B), leaving any change to the retained runs unresolved.

E4.justification: Table 3 newly tests fixed versus increasing parallelism for confidence and random selection. Appendix A.2/Table 5 separately tests block size at fixed computation. Figure 1 also adds a GSM8K reasoning-trace case study. V1 contains none of these analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Average NFE describes decoding computation rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the original three models' GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP scores, while adding MATH500 and DiffuCoder results. Tables 2, 3, and 5 add further outcomes; for example, Table 2 reports BBH accuracy of 40.56% for DUS versus 35.93% for confidence with LLaDA-Base at B=32. These are additional results, not improvements over corresponding v1 runs.

T1.justification: V3 reorganizes the existing entropy approximation and MI-decay argument into two lemmas and revises the derivation. Equation 12 replaces v1 Equation 11's dependence on the first selected token with the preceding selected token, separates the initial entropy term, and changes the error allocation from epsilon/k to epsilon/(k−1). The underlying Markov and fast-mixing assumptions remain.

C1.justification: The training-free, logarithmic DUS contribution remains. V3 extends the empirical superiority claim to general knowledge, explicitly frames a speed–quality tradeoff, and narrows the introduction's theoretical claim from preserving/improving output quality to approaching an entropy bound under fast mixing. The conclusion's quoted maximum gain changes from 'up to 5' to 'up to 27%'.

C2.justification: V3 newly interprets uniform parallelism as preferable for confidence selection and increasing parallelism as beneficial for random sampling. Appendix A.2 explains block-size effects through token spacing and adds a limitation concerning insufficient local context at excessive block sizes. Its claimed monotonic improvement overlooks Table 5's Base-model dip from 13.33% to 11.00%.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands reproducibility information: V100 hardware, the evaluation harness and upstream implementation, benchmark sample counts, prompting shot counts, subset selection, and a custom MATH500 task implementation. The previously stated generation lengths and EOS stopping condition are retained.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially expands positioning around speculative decoding, EB-Sampler, DiffuCoder, FreeCache, dKV-Cache, and commercial diffusion systems. It adds corresponding citations and comparisons of their approaches with DUS, while dropping some earlier references, including the remasking work by Wang et al.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, related work becomes a separate section, and the method is reorganized into numbered subsections separating notation, formulation, scheduling, and theory. Experiments gain distinct analysis subsections and an appendix, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a full-width composite with new colored token-trace panels alongside retained benchmark plots. Table 1 is reorganized from model-specific subtables into a consolidated dataset/model matrix with block sizes across columns. Four additional tables present benchmarks, ablations, and notation.

improvement.justification: The new ablations investigate scheduling and block-size effects, while Appendix A.1 supplies evaluation details missing from v1, improving empirical support and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by conflicting token-budget formulas, different semi-AR settings in the DiffuCoder comparison, and interpretations contradicted by new results, including Table 1's outperformance exceptions and Table 5's nonmonotonic Base scores.
